title: Arguments by register
description:
Say where each argument of a function lives under the Windows x64 calling convention.

```
int f(int a, double b, char* c, int d, int e)
a -> ecx, b -> xmm1, c -> r8, d -> r9d, e -> [rsp+0x28]
return -> eax
```
hints: The position decides the slot, whatever the earlier types: a `double` second goes in `xmm1`, not `xmm0` (lesson 2.01).
At the call, `[rsp]` is the return address and `rsp+8` to `rsp+0x20` is the shadow space.
requirements: The first four arguments use one slot each: rcx/xmm0, rdx/xmm1, r8/xmm2, r9/xmm3 by position.
Later arguments go on the stack after the 32-byte shadow space: `[rsp+0x28]`, `[rsp+0x30]`, ...
Pick the register size by type (`ecx` for an `int`, `rcx` for a pointer).
stretch: Add the Linux System V rules, where integers and floats use separate counters.
